name: @askturret/mcp-adapter-test
description: MCP adapter conformance kit - run the shared test bank against any framework adapter

askturret.versioning: TWO VERSIONS, DELIBERATELY INDEPENDENT, and the distinction is the point. `version` is this npm package's semver and tracks the project like any other workspace. KIT_VERSION is the CONFORMANCE-RESULT CONTRACT: it moves when the categories change or an existing one gets stricter, never because a release happened, so a stored result stays meaningful alongside the kit version that produced it. They were the same string (1.0.0) while this package was private and `version` was inert; publishing made `version` load-bearing, so it was set to 0.1.0 — a 0.x project shipping a 1.0.0 package on day one would promise a stability it does not have. Precedent: the plugin apiVersion in compatibility-policy.md §2.
askturret.publishing: PUBLIC as of #173. `private: false` in this manifest is the authority, and `npm view @askturret/mcp-adapter-test` is how to check from outside. Some workspaces in this repo publish and some do not — read each manifest's `private` field rather than assuming the repo is uniform. This package's runtime dependency @askturret/mcp-adapter-conformance is published alongside it in the same change; publishing this one without that one would 404 on its own dependency. The decision was made in architecture §12.2 and #54, whose acceptance is `published on npm`, and was sequenced behind the first @askturret/mcp-core release, which shipped as 0.2.0.
